lead.headline: Wall Street has its worst day since June as Intel falls 28% and fears grow that AI spending will not pay off
lead.short: Tech shares fell for a second day on Friday, dragging Wall Street to its worst day since June. Intel lost about 28%, more than $130bn in value, after a weak forecast, and Alphabet fell another 1.4% after Thursday's 12% plunge. The Nasdaq-100 fell 3.5% and ended October with its worst month since March 2025.

why.text: Indian IT and chip-linked shares trade on the same AI story, and a rout in New York usually reaches Mumbai on Monday.

more: Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon and Microsoft have committed about $800bn between them to spending this year, much of it on AI, but earnings are not always matching. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue of $15bn to $16bn against forecasts of about $17bn, and no positive cash flow; chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said AI's appetite for memory is pushing up PC prices and slowing sales.

Amazon said it had spent more cash than it made, and plans $220bn of spending this year. Gold fell 3.5% to a one-year low of about $3,881 an ounce as metals were dragged down too. OpenAI has raised about $11bn of a $30bn funding target, The Wall Street Journal reports.

update.new: The sell-off spread: Intel's worst day, and Wall Street's worst since June.
update.front: What began with Alphabet has become a broad rout, the market's sharpest doubt yet about AI spending.

seconds.headline: A tanker carrying 27 Indian seafarers is hit by limpet mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and all are safe
seconds.short: The Panama-flagged crude tanker MT Louise 1, with 27 Indian crew, was struck by limpet mines on Thursday about 46 km northeast of Oman's Khasab, causing a fire. All the Indians are safe and unhurt, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said. Two Indians aboard a second tanker, the Liberia-flagged MT Arzanah, hit by a projectile, are also safe.

why.text: Thousands of Indian sailors crew ships through Hormuz, and 22 Indians have already died in the West Asia war, 14 of them seafarers.

more: A small boat attached two limpet mines to the Louise 1's hull, three maritime sources told Reuters, in the first reported successful use of such explosives in the waterway since the war began; an attempt in September failed to detonate. It was not immediately clear who was responsible.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said four tankers caught fire and exploded in the strait while using what it called unauthorised routes. Tehran has largely blocked the strait since the US-Israeli strikes in February, and the US has struck Iran-linked tankers under its naval blockade. A draft US-Iran framework would reopen Hormuz within seven days of a first deal, Al Arabiya reports.

facts.place: about 46 km northeast of Khasab, Oman

update.new: Limpet mines hit a tanker with 27 Indians aboard; all are safe.
update.front: It is the first successful mine attack on a ship in Hormuz in the war, and 27 Indian lives were at stake.

seconds.headline: The US scraps the G20 foreign ministers' family photo after Europeans refuse to pose with Russia's Lavrov
seconds.short: Marco Rubio cancelled the traditional group photo at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on Friday after several Europeans threatened to boycott it or walk out rather than be pictured with Russia's Sergey Lavrov. The talks went ahead, and Rubio appealed for unity, calling it "a moment of choosing" for the United States and for the world.

why.text: The G20 is one of the few forums where India sits with all the big powers, and the photo row shows how divided it has become.

more: "We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises," Rubio said, pointing to disruption to energy and food supplies, trade and shipping. There was no sign of consensus on the Ukraine war, the US-Israeli war on Iran, US tariffs or China's moves in the South China Sea.

Some members had objected to the US inviting Russia while it steps up attacks on Ukraine, after Trump waived new sanctions on Moscow and briefly limited help to Kyiv. Britain said it has a longstanding policy of no direct bilateral engagement with Russian ministers since the invasion, "and we are not about to change that".

facts.objection: European ministers would not be photographed with Lavrov

seconds.headline: Riot police guard Poland's top court after a judge suspends its president, and the president flies home to cries of a coup
seconds.short: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal announced on Friday evening that its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and vice-president had been suspended by the longest-serving judge, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who said she was restoring the rule of law. The court's own account called it a coup. President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane round on the way to Senegal, and riot police surrounded the court.

why.text: Poland is the EU's sixth-biggest economy and a frontline NATO state, and its fight over the courts now has police on the steps.

more: "At a moment like this, the President must be in Poland," Nawrocki wrote on X. Early on Saturday he entered the tribunal building with the First President of the Supreme Court, Zbigniew Kapinski, his chief of staff, Pawel Szefernaker, said on X. Dozens of protesters gathered outside, some chanting "Tusk traitor" against Donald Tusk's pro-European government.

The tribunal's X account said Korwin-Piotrowska "is not a judge of the Constitutional Tribunal" and that everyone involved was committing the crime of a coup d'état. The court's website went down shortly after the notice appeared. Poland's ambassador to China, Jakub Kumoch, resigned over the events.

facts.president: Karol Nawrocki returned from a trip to Senegal

seconds.headline: A German and a Slovak die of electrocution in the pool of Bengaluru's Conrad hotel, and two rescuers are hurt
seconds.short: Alexander Maximilian Theiss, 57, a German Lufthansa crew member, and Juraj Horvat, 45, a Slovak IBM project manager, died after being electrocuted in the third-floor pool of the Conrad hotel in Ulsoor on Friday evening. An American guest and the hotel's lifeguard were hurt trying to save them. Police have registered a case.

why.text: It is a basic safety failure at one of the city's top hotels, and the police inquiry will decide who is held responsible.

more: "The cause of death was electrocution," said Dr Mabel Vasnaik, head of emergency medicine at Manipal Hospitals. Theiss was brought in dead, and doctors tried and failed to revive Horvat. The American, Mathew Desantis, 41, felt a current while swimming and got out; the lifeguard, Rahul Tiwari, 28, jumped in to save the other two.

Both survivors are stable and were expected to be discharged on Saturday, though Tiwari is being checked for fractures. The American had complained of a headache, doctors said. Police say they are investigating how the pool became live. The hotel is on the third floor of the building in Ulsoor, near the lake.

stories.headline: A tampered Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace put a backdoor on up to 5,000 developers' machines for nearly 12 hours
stories.short: An attacker published a tampered version of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, version 2.1.313, through Anthropic's verified account on the Cursor marketplace, and it reached at most 5,000 users, Cursor said on Friday. It tried to install a hidden SSH backdoor. Anthropic says it did not build or publish the copy, and pushed a clean version hours later.

why.text: Coding tools now run with full access to developers' machines, so a single poisoned update can open thousands of companies' code.

more: The malicious extension added an attacker's SSH key, turned on the local SSH service and opened a reverse tunnel, on Windows, macOS and Linux, Cursor said. Because extensions run with the editor's permissions, it could reach source code and stored credentials. Bugs in the code stopped it working on some Windows and Mac machines.

"It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel," said Luke Roberts of the security firm Phorion. Extensions update automatically in Cursor by default. Neither company has explained how the account was taken over; researcher Kevin Beaumont said the clean version, 2.1.314, followed several hours later.

briefs.text: Teghaza 001 is only the third ancient Martian meteorite known, a NASA-led team found. Most Martian rocks on Earth are 2.4 billion years old or younger.

update.new: A Saharan meteorite is dated to Mars's ancient crust.

stories.headline: Mbappé lost the Ballon d'Or to Kane by just 28 points, the full voting shows, with Bellingham 11th
stories.short: The full Ballon d'Or voting shows Harry Kane scored 1,055 points to Kylian Mbappé's 1,027, the fourth-closest finish between the top two in the award's history. Kane had 40 first-place votes to Mbappé's 23. Lamine Yamal was third with 881. Jude Bellingham was 11th, Vinícius Júnior 17th and Marc Cucurella 18th.

why.text: Mbappé came within a whisker of football's top prize in a season that has turned into a China crisis.

more: Rodri was fourth with 726 points, ahead of Lionel Messi on 612, and PSG's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Ousmane Dembélé were sixth and seventh. Bellingham's 107 points left him just outside the top 10, while Vinícius had 26 and Cucurella 16.

Madrid visit Racing Santander on Sunday. A former Madrid technical secretary, Miguel Ángel Portugal, says an intermediary once offered the club a teenage Lionel Messi, before he had a professional contract at Barcelona. Kane became the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001. Mbappé had been among the favourites going into the ceremony, and the figures put a number on his disappointment.

update.new: The full voting: Mbappé lost by 28 points.

stories.headline: Verstappen and Lawson each get a one-place grid penalty for a 'clumsy' clash in practice, as Leclerc tops Friday in Mexico
stories.short: Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson will each lose a grid place in Mexico City after they collided at Turn 12 in second practice, damaging the Red Bull's floor and the Racing Bulls' front wing and causing a red flag. The stewards called it unacceptable after a warning to teams that morning. Charles Leclerc was fastest on Friday.

why.text: Kimi Antonelli is champion on Sunday unless George Russell wins, and any grid change near the front matters.

more: "Both drivers admitted the moves were unnecessary and 'clumsy'," the stewards wrote, escalating from a warning to a grid penalty because of similar incidents this year. Lawson said Verstappen "literally drove into me"; Verstappen criticised Lawson for "not very smart behaviour". Racing Bulls' Alan Permane called it "completely unnecessary".

Ten drivers sat out the first session to give rookies track time. Leclerc beat Lando Norris and George Russell in the second, while Lewis Hamilton was told to stop his Ferrari on track with a problem. Verstappen finished fifth in the session and Lawson ninth. The race starts at 01:30 IST on Monday.

update.new: Practice: Leclerc fastest; Verstappen and Lawson penalised.
